raw_response.overlap_rationale: Both full texts are complete and match their respective citations. Study A (Seneviratne 2000) examines urban water supply, sanitation, tariff cross-subsidization, and public utility performance in Sri Lanka (focusing on Greater Colombo, Kandy, Galle, Jaffna, Puttalam, and 275 water supply schemes across 24 Sri Lankan districts using 1985–1998 sector reports). Study B (Molinos-Senante 2018) is a book chapter analyzing legal reforms, utility privatization, hypothetical efficient-company tariff regulation, and service quality benchmarking across 28 urban water and sanitation companies in Chile regulated by the Superintendencia de Servicios Sanitarios (SISS) using 1998–2015 administrative data. The two studies have different authors, continents, decades, institutional settings, and underlying data sources (likely flagged as a candidate pair only because both titles feature 'Urban Water Management' and both start on page 131).
raw_response.study_a_sample_and_data: Sector-wide policy and institutional review of urban water supply and sanitation in Sri Lanka (urban population 3.8 million in 1998, with emphasis on Greater Colombo, Kandy, Galle, Jaffna, and Puttalam), drawing on 1985–1998 government and donor reports (NWSDB, Presidential Task Force 1995, OECF/JICA 1997, ADB 1998) covering 275 water supply schemes across 24 districts in 1997, projected Colombo water demand (1995–2020), capital investment scenarios, and NWSDB rising-block tariffs.
raw_response.study_b_sample_and_data: National regulatory and sector performance review of urban water and sanitation services in Chile (16,812,391 urban residents served by 28 main private and concessionary water companies, plus 278 wastewater treatment systems), synthesizing administrative and benchmarking data from the national regulator Superintendencia de Servicios Sanitarios (SISS) spanning 1998–2015 (principally 2007–2015 quality indicators, tariffs, Casen-targeted household subsidies, and non-revenue water).
